title: Others with Baron: pious affection must precede assent (Ames)
source_text: VIII. Contra tamen sentiunt praestantes alii Scholae Reformatae Doctores, & cum Rob. Baronio docent ad fidei assensum praerequiri motum & affectum aliquem voluntatis, quo mens ad assentiendum veritatibus fidei impellatur. Id manifeste colligitur ex Amesii doctrina. Nam inter ea quae praecedunt assensum, quem veritati divinae praebemus, unum est, juxta ipsum, Affectio pia erga Deum, quae facit ut maxime valeat apud nos ipsius testimonium. In Medulla Theol. lib. 1. cap. 5.
pass_a_gloss: Yet other outstanding Reformed Doctors think otherwise, and with Robert Baron teach that for faith's assent some motion and affection of the will is presupposed, by which the mind is driven to assent to faith's truths. This is clearly gathered from Ames's teaching. For among the things that precede the assent we give to divine truth, one is, according to him, a pious affection toward God, which makes His testimony weigh most with us (Medulla Theol. 1.5).
pass_b_english: Baron's side: some will-affection must precede assent.
Ames: pious affection toward God is among assent's antecedents (Medulla 1.5).

choices.why: Required before assent, not identical with it.
